catalogue.name: Inventory.PhysInventory.RecordCount
catalogue.description: Records counted quantities on lines of a physical inventory journal; an omitted quantity leaves the count unchanged and zero counts as counted zero.
catalogue.selectionDescription: Identify one existing nonrecurring Phys. Inventory journal batch using templateName/batchName or subject TEMPLATE|BATCH or SystemId. All supplied selectors must agree.

subject.description: Identifies the journal batch as TEMPLATE|BATCH, or as the SystemId of the Item Journal Batch. Without a subject, send templateName and batchName in data. Every selector that is sent must name the same batch.

target.description: The journal template name and the batch name, each at most 10 characters, separated by a vertical bar. The template must be a Phys. Inventory template that is not recurring.
The SystemId of the Item Journal Batch.
The template and the batch together. data.journalTemplateName and data.journalBatchName are accepted as aliases.

parameters.name: templateName
parameters.description: Name of an existing Phys. Inventory journal template that is not recurring, at most 10 characters. Send it with batchName unless subject identifies the batch.

parameters.name: batchName
parameters.description: Name of an existing journal batch of that template, at most 10 characters. Every selector that is sent must name the same batch.

parameters.name: journalTemplateName
parameters.description: Alias of templateName. A value that differs from templateName, ignoring case, is refused.

parameters.name: journalBatchName
parameters.description: Alias of batchName. A value that differs from batchName, ignoring case, is refused.

parameters.name: counts
parameters.description: Nonempty array of counted lines. Each entry names one line of the batch and optionally the counted quantity. The lines must be distinct. Required by Inventory.PhysInventory.RecordCount; Inventory.PhysInventory.Record may send lineNo and quantity instead.

children.name: lineNo
children.description: Positive line number in the batch. Send lineNo or systemId; when both are sent they must name the same line.

children.name: systemId
children.description: SystemId of the journal line, which must belong to the batch.

children.name: qtyCounted
children.description: Counted quantity, zero or more. Zero is written as a counted zero. Omit it to leave the line unchanged.

parameters.name: lineNo
parameters.description: Inventory.PhysInventory.Record only, when counts is absent: positive line number of the line to count. Refused by Inventory.PhysInventory.RecordCount.

parameters.name: quantity
parameters.description: Inventory.PhysInventory.Record only, when counts is absent: counted quantity, zero or more. Omit it to leave the line unchanged. Refused by Inventory.PhysInventory.RecordCount.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Success when every count was applied.

fields.name: templateName
fields.description: The journal template of the selected batch.

fields.name: result
fields.description: One entry per counted line, in the order of counts.

children.name: counted
children.description: True when qtyCounted was sent for the line; false when the line was left unchanged.

children.name: adjustmentQuantity
children.description: Adjustment quantity of the line after the count.

fields.name: lineNo
fields.description: Inventory.PhysInventory.Record only: line number of the last counted line.

fields.name: quantity
fields.description: Inventory.PhysInventory.Record only: counted quantity of the last counted line.

fields.name: quantityCalculated
fields.description: Inventory.PhysInventory.Record only: calculated quantity of the last counted line.

errors.when: Inventory.PhysInventory.Record only: journalTemplateName (or templateName), journalBatchName (or batchName) and lineNo are sent in data and name a journal line that does not exist.
errors.fix: Check the batch and lineNo, or run Inventory.PhysInventory.Calculate first.

errors.when: The Physical Inventory domain is turned off for this company in Inventory Setup.
errors.fix: Turn the domain on from the Inventory Setup page.

errors.when: The caller has no write permission on the Item Journal Line table.
errors.fix: Ask an administrator for a permission set that grants it, for example the Bifrost "Full Access" permission set.

errors.error: counts must contain distinct journal lines identified by lineNo or systemId; qtyCounted must be a nonnegative number when present.
errors.when: counts is absent, not an array or empty, an entry is not an object or names a line outside the batch, a line is repeated, lineNo and systemId name different lines, or qtyCounted is negative or not a number. Nothing is changed.
errors.fix: Send a nonempty counts array of distinct lines of the batch.

errors.when: A key is sent that this type does not read, including a key inside a counts entry, or lineNo and quantity at the top level of Inventory.PhysInventory.RecordCount.
errors.fix: Remove the key; Inventory.PhysInventory.RecordCount takes counts only.

errors.error: Identify one existing journal batch using templateName and batchName or subject TEMPLATE|BATCH or SystemId.
errors.when: No batch is identified, the selectors name different batches, the subject is neither TEMPLATE|BATCH nor a SystemId, the batch does not exist, or its template is not a Phys. Inventory template or is recurring.
errors.fix: Identify one existing batch of a non-recurring Phys. Inventory template with consistent selectors.

errors.when: A line is not a valid physical inventory line, or Business Central refuses the counted quantity. Every count of the call is rolled back.
errors.fix: Correct the line or the quantity named in the text and retry.

errors.when: A transient lock or deadlock caught while writing or posting. The error preserves Business Central's original text. Uncaught errors are Retryable only for types with effect write.
errors.fix: Retry the same call after a few seconds; nothing was changed.

effect.changes: Sets the counted quantity, Qty. (Phys. Inventory), on each line named in counts that has a qtyCounted, through the standard validation; Business Central then recalculates the adjustment quantity and entry type of the line. Lines without qtyCounted are left unchanged. Nothing is posted. The changes are committed with the answer; under Omit Commit the caller's transaction commits instead.

related.name: Inventory.PhysInventory.Calculate
related.useInsteadWhen: Use it to create the lines of an empty batch before counting.

related.name: Inventory.PhysInventory.Check
related.useInsteadWhen: Use it to find line problems after the counts are entered.

related.name: Inventory.PhysInventory.PreviewPost
related.useInsteadWhen: Use it to see the entries a posting would create.

related.name: Inventory.PhysInventory.Post
related.useInsteadWhen: Use it to post the counted lines.

steps.purpose: Create the lines of an empty batch from the expected stock.
Enter the counted quantity on each line.
Post the count; the adjustments are written to the ledger.

examples.title: Record a counted quantity of zero on line 10000

chapters.overview: Sets the counted quantity on lines of a Phys. Inventory journal batch, for both Inventory.PhysInventory.RecordCount and the legacy Inventory.PhysInventory.Record. An entry without qtyCounted leaves its line unchanged, zero is written as counted zero, and nothing is posted.
chapters.notes: This help describes two types that share one implementation: Inventory.PhysInventory.RecordCount takes counts; the legacy type Inventory.PhysInventory.Record takes the same counts or, when counts is absent, one line as lineNo plus quantity. The two differ only where this text says so. Only counted quantities are written; nothing is posted. Every counts entry is validated before any line changes and the call is atomic: if one entry fails, no line is changed. An entry without qtyCounted leaves its line unchanged, and zero is written as a counted zero. The lines must be distinct lines of the batch, and each must be a valid physical inventory line. After the count is set Business Central recalculates the adjustment quantity (adjustmentQuantity) and the entry type of the line; result reports before, after, quantityCalculated and adjustmentQuantity per line. Inventory.PhysInventory.RecordCount refuses lineNo and quantity at the top level as unsupported keys. Inventory.PhysInventory.Record adds lineNo, quantity and quantityCalculated of the last counted line to the answer, and answers InvalidParameter for lineNo when data names a template, a batch and a lineNo that do not exist. Any other key is refused. The counts are committed with the answer; under Omit Commit the caller's transaction commits instead. Under Omit Commit an error is raised to the caller instead of being answered with the error text. The Physical Inventory domain must be turned on in Inventory Setup (a missing setup row counts as on) and the caller needs write permission on the Item Journal Line table. Use Inventory.PhysInventory.Calculate first to create the lines and Inventory.PhysInventory.Check afterwards.

result.conventions:
## Errors and warnings
An error response has `status` = `Error`, a stable `code`, the `error` text and, when they apply, `parameter` (the request parameter concerned, e.g. `lines[2].no`), `received` (the value received), `expected` (what was expected) and `nextStep` (what to do now). `hint` says where to read more.
When a request has several problems, all of them are listed in `errors[]` - each with the same fields - under a top-level `code` (`MultipleErrors`, or a shared code such as `InvalidLine` for the `lines` of a Create type) and a summary `error`. Fix them all before calling again. One problem is reported at the top level, with no `errors[]`.
Request values are checked first and every problem found is reported together. A Business Central validation error raised afterwards, while a record is being written, stops the call and is reported on its own: `code` = `BusinessCentralError`, Business Central's own `error` text, and `parameter` naming the request parameter being applied, e.g. `lines[1].accountNo`. Nothing is written.
Request values are read in one format, whatever the language: dates `YYYY-MM-DD`; date-times ISO 8601 with `Z` or an offset; amounts as JSON numbers (or a string such as `"1234.56"`, no thousands separator); integers as JSON integers; booleans `true` or `false`. Any other value is `InvalidParameterFormat` with `received` and `expected`; for an unambiguous local form such as `26.09.2026`, `nextStep` gives the value to resend. Every bad value of a request is reported together.
Answers are written in one format as well, whatever the language of the call: dates `YYYY-MM-DD`, date-times ISO 8601, numbers with a dot and no thousands separator, and the option and enum values of every answer except `Data.Records.Get` and `Data.Records.Set` as their English names, so a value read from an answer can be sent back. Those two answer the caption of the language of the call, for a person to read. The language of the call (`lcid`) changes captions and message texts, not these forms. Two things are outside Bifrost's control: Business Central writes its own texts (a ledger entry description such as `Direct Cost V00010 on 10/02/26`, the text of a `BusinessCentralError`) with the regional settings of the server session, which `lcid` does not change, so a date in such a text can be in month-day order; and a table view is read with those settings too, so write dates in a view as `YYYY-MM-DD` and decimals with a dot.
Both success and error responses can carry `warnings[]`, each with `code`, `message` and, when they apply, `parameter` and `nextStep`.
`UnknownParameter` refuses undeclared data keys before execution for every type whose effect is not read, including a missing effect. The root envelope option `strict:false` cannot opt out. Read types keep warnings without changing status, validationResult or domain warningCount unless the caller sets `strict:true` (next to type and subject, never inside data). Refusals list the keys and localized nextStep corrections; no business changes or successful execution charges occur. Example: {"type":"Memory.User.Set","strict":true,"data":{"memory":"test","memry":"typo"}} is refused.
`FieldChangedByBC` is a warning from Data.Records.Set: another field validation or the write changed a sent field after its own validation. `parameter` names data[n].fields.{jsonName}, counting from 0. Status stays Success. Compare the returned values with what you sent; follow `nextStep` to use validation order or send the field again in a separate call. Normalisation of the field itself, LCY, Dimension Set ID, BLOB, Media, MediaSet and skipped fields are excluded.
When a Business Central operation fails, the error can identify the request parameter being applied, the expected input and what to do next. That guidance accompanies the original `BusinessCentralError` after rollback, including a failed queued task. It does not change which writes are rolled back or committed. Guidance is cleared between messages; a message without it keeps its existing response shape. Recognized lock errors follow the `Retryable` rules below.
Some message types accept calls only through a particular path: a scheduled queue message, the Task API (`/tasks`), the in-product MCP tool server, another message type, or the Messages page Run Task action. Bifrost determines where the call came from; request values cannot override it. A call through an unsupported path is refused with `PreconditionFailed` and a `nextStep` naming the path to use.
`Retryable` means a transient lock or deadlock caught while writing or posting. `error` keeps Business Central's original text. `expected` is "no concurrent lock on the same records"; `nextStep` is "Retry the same call after a few seconds; nothing was changed." Bifrost does not retry automatically. Uncaught recognized lock errors are also `Retryable` for `write` types. Uncaught `read` and `irreversible` errors remain `BusinessCentralError`, because an irreversible operation may already have committed.
`ConfirmationRequired` is the preview refusal for an irreversible type called without `expectedCount`. Nothing was changed; inspect `expected` and the description before sending the same request with that count. `ConfirmationMismatch` means the count has changed or the sent count was wrong; nothing was changed. Inspect the new preview before confirming again. Feature apps use the same preview and confirmation protocol for irreversible operations.
Codes: `MissingParameter`, `InvalidParameterFormat`, `InvalidParameter`, `RecordNotFound`, `AmbiguousRecord`, `ConflictingIdentifiers`, `InvalidFilterField`, `InvalidLine`, `NothingToPreview`, `LinesSkipped`, `BlockedByWriteGuard`, `PreconditionFailed`, `PermissionDenied`, `LimitExceeded`, `BusinessCentralError`, `MultipleErrors`, `DeprecatedParameter`, `UnknownParameter`, `FieldChangedByBC`, `Retryable`, `EULA_REQUIRED`, `TRIAL_NOT_STARTED`, `ConfirmationRequired`, `ConfirmationMismatch`. The `error` text may be translated; the code never is.
